source_text: Et merces aduenient meritis partita locorum. Inde tamen pergit uictor in terra Iudaea, Quem ipsi Iudaei expectant uincere Roma<m> Multa signa facit, ut illi credere possint, Ad seducendos eos quoniam est missus iniquus; Quem tamen e caelo increpat uox reddita Summi. De Persida homo immortalem esse se dicit. Nobis Nero factus Antichristus, ille Iudaeis; Isti duo semper prophetae sunt in ultima fine. Urbis perditio Nero est, hic terrae totius; De quo pauca tamen suggero, quae legi secreta. Displicet interea iam sero Iudaeis et ipsis, Susurrantque simul, quoniam sint fraude decepti. Exclamant pariter ad caelum uoce deflentes, Tunc Deus omnipotens, terminet ut cuncta, quae dixi, Producet populum celatum tempore multo. Sunt autem Iudaei trans Persida flumine clausi, Quos usque in finem uoluit Deus ibi morari. Captiuitas illos ibidem redegit ut essent; Ex duodena tribu noue<m> semis ibi morantur. Mendacium ibi non est, sed nec est odium ullum; Idcirco nec moritur filius suus ante parentes; Nec mortuos plangunt nec lugunt more de nostro, Expectant quoniam resurrectionemque futuram, Non animam ullam uescuntur additis escis, Sed olera tantum, quod sit sine sanguine fuso. Iustitia pleni illibato corpore uiuunt, In illis nec genesis exercit impia uires. Non febres accedunt in illis, non frigora saeua, Obtemperant quoniam uniuersa candide legis; Quae nos et ipsi sequemur pure uiuentes; Mors tantum aderat et labor, nam cetera surda. Hic erat populus, qui nunc est extra repositus. Siccato fluuio repetet in terra Iudaea; Cum ipsis et Deus ueniet implere promissa; Qui per totum iter exultat Deo praesente. Omnia uirescunt ante illos, omnia gaudent, Excipere sanctos ipsa creatura laetatur: Omni loco fontes exurgunt esse parati, Qua graditur populus Summi cum terrore caelesti.
pass_a_gloss: Merces locorum. Victor in Iudaea — seductor signis. Nero nobis Antichristus, ille Iudaeis. Clamor decepti. Populus clausus trans Persida — iusti, sine odio, resurrectio.
pass_b_english: And wages will arrive parted by deserts of places. From there nonetheless the victor proceeds into the Judean land, whom the Jews themselves expect to conquer Rome. He makes many signs, that they may be able to believe him, since the unjust one is sent to seduce them; whom nonetheless a voice returned from heaven of the Highest rebukes. A man from Persia says that he himself is immortal. To us Nero has become Antichrist, that one to the Jews; these two always are prophets at the last end. The city’s ruin is Nero, this one’s the whole earth’s; about whom nonetheless I offer a few things that I have read secret. Meanwhile he displeases the Jews too late even themselves, and they whisper together that they have been deceived by fraud. They cry alike to heaven with weeping voice; then God almighty, that he may end all things I have said, will bring forth a people hidden for a long time. But there are Jews shut beyond Persia by a river, whom God willed to stay there even to the end. Captivity drove them there that they might be; from the twelve tribes nine and a half stay there. There is no lie there, nor is there any hatred; therefore neither does a son die before his parents; nor do they mourn the dead nor grieve in our manner, since they await the resurrection to come; they feed on no soul with added foods, but only herbs, which may be without blood poured. Full of justice they live with unstained body; in them neither does an impious birth exercise forces. Fevers do not approach them, nor savage colds, since they obey all things of the law brightly; which we too ourselves will follow living purely; death only was present and toil, for the rest were mute. This was the people that now is stored away outside. With the river dried he will seek again into the Judean land; with them God also will come to fill promises; who through the whole journey exults with God present. All things grow green before them, all things rejoice; creation itself is glad to receive the holy: in every place springs rise ready to be, where the people of the Highest walks with heavenly awe. ****** Two end-liars: Nero for us, the Persian wonder for the Jews. God then leads out the sealed, bloodless, law-bright people from beyond the river.
